name: Vespid Dynamics Neural Hornet NH-1 'Brainbug'
description: A micro-drone the size of a large insect that autonomously navigates to a target's head and delivers a neural disruption payload through a penetrating proboscis. The NH-1 uses thermal and pheromone tracking to identify and approach a specific individual, then lands on exposed skin — typically the neck or behind the ear — and inserts a 2mm probe that delivers a concentrated electromagnetic pulse directly to the neural interface hardware. The target experiences immediate sensory overload, disorientation, and temporary loss of motor control. The drone then self-destructs, leaving minimal forensic evidence. Vespid does not acknowledge the NH-1's existence in any product catalog.
legality: Does not officially exist — no legal classification
specifications:
drone size: 3 cm wingspan
flight time: 8 minutes
tracking: Thermal signature + pheromone profile matching
proboscis penetration: 2mm subcutaneous
payload: Focused micro-EMP to neural interface
self-destruct: Thermite micro-charge, 2 seconds post-delivery
weight: 4 grams
operating range: 200 meters from launch point
story_hooks: A corporate executive collapsed during a public speech with symptoms consistent with neural interface overload — a dead insect-sized drone was found crushed on their collar.
Someone has obtained NH-1 pheromone tracking data and is selling target-locked drones to anyone with the money — assassination as a subscription service.

physical_description.visual_profile: A biomimetic micro-drone engineered to resemble a large hornet or wasp. Sleek, predatory silhouette with a tapered fuselage and articulated wings. The body appears almost organic despite its synthetic construction — a deliberately unsettling fusion of insect anatomy and lethal technology. At 3cm wingspan, it's distinctly larger than a natural hornet but maintains a profile designed to avoid immediate recognition as a weapon.
physical_description.weight_description: Feather-light at 4 grams — practically negligible in hand, creating an eerie sense of lethality despite its insubstantial feel. The weight distribution is fore-heavy due to the proboscis mechanism and payload chamber.
physical_description.primary_material: Reinforced bio-polymer exoskeleton with segmented carbon-fiber joints. The thorax housing contains quantum-hardened aluminum alloy for the penetration mechanism and thermite charge.
physical_description.finish: Matte chitinous appearance with a slight iridescent sheen under certain light angles — mimicking natural insect carapace. The wing membranes are translucent synthetic material with faint vein-like conductive tracery visible when backlit.
physical_description.color_scheme: Primary mottled charcoal-grey with amber-gold accents along the wing leading edges and around the launch aperture. The proboscis tip has a faint violet tint from neural-resonant coating.
physical_description.grip_texture: Not designed for hand-gripping — the NH-1 launches from a compact magnetic-release pod. The pod itself has a smooth, recessed grip surface of rubberized polymer.
distinctive_features: Retractable 2mm penetrating proboscis housed in the anterior fuselage — barely visible when stowed
Compound optical sensors mimicking insect facet eyes (likely thermal+visual hybrid arrays)
Pheromone-detection antennae — articulated, hair-thin conductive filaments extending from the head
Micro-thruster vents along the abdomen — almost invisible but create faint heat distortion
Faint LED status indicator (amber/red) recessed into the dorsal surface near the wing root
Segmented abdomen designed to contain thermite micro-charge — slightly bulbous compared to real insects
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: None visible. Vespid Dynamics officially denies existence. Underground markets report micro-etched serial codes on the fuselage interior (not visible without disassembly), a dark joke among users.
physical_description.condition_typical: Field units appear fresh from manufacture — matte finish unmarred, wings pristine. Battle-worn units are rare (self-destruct leaves minimal recovery). When recovered intact, signs of pheromone residue around antennae or minor thermal discoloration on the fuselage indicate activation.

Shot from slightly above at 45-degree angle.
